restated_task: Implement the is_balanced(s) function in brackets/core.py to check if a string has balanced and properly nested brackets of three types: (), [], {}. Non-bracket characters are ignored. The function must return a boolean (True for balanced, False otherwise). It must raise TypeError if the input is not a string. The existing is_bracket helper function and the test suite must not be modified.

interface_contract.name: is_bracket
interface_contract.behavior: Returns True if c is a single-character string and one of the six bracket characters '(', ')', '[', ']', '{', '}'. Returns False otherwise (including for non-strings, empty strings, or strings of length >1).

interface_contract.name: is_balanced
interface_contract.behavior: Returns True if all brackets in the string s are correctly matched and properly nested, ignoring any non-bracket characters. Returns False if brackets are unmatched, incorrectly nested, or if there are extra closing or opening brackets. The empty string returns True.
error_cases: TypeError: raised when s is not a string.

acceptance_criteria: 15. Non-bracket characters are ignored: is_balanced('a') returns True, is_balanced('(a') returns False, is_balanced('a)') returns False.
16. is_balanced returns a bool (True or False) for all string inputs.
17. is_balanced raises TypeError when s is not a string (e.g., None, 123, [], {}).
18. Existing is_bracket behavior is preserved: is_bracket(c) returns True for each of '(', ')', '[', ']', '{', '}' and False for any other input.
out_of_scope: Do not modify the is_bracket function.
Do not modify the test files (tests/test_basic.py).
Do not change the PAIRS, OPEN, CLOSE constants unless necessary for the implementation (but they are provided and should be used).
